supporting_observations.claim: At 13:37:45 UTC, Kerberos events show requests for a TGT for raj.patel and a service ticket for WS-RPATEL-01 from 10.51.10.21; shortly afterward, WS-RPATEL-01 recorded a network logon for raj.patel from that same IP. The inventory identifies 10.51.10.21 as WS-ARUIZ-01, and says remote administration is only performed from WS-RPATEL-01. This is suspicious and inconsistent with the stated practice, but does not establish that it caused the reported PowerShell window.

At 13:44 UTC, a request authenticated as ana.ruiz retrieved https://raw.githubusercontent.com/pinecrest-it/tools/main/u.ps1 with status 200 from WS-ARUIZ-01. This is relevant to the PowerShell alert, but the record does not show the script contents or that it was executed.
The available records do not establish what process, if any, produced the reported PowerShell window around 13:40 UTC.

known_telemetry_limitations: Winsec and Sysmon collection for WS-ARUIZ-01 was unavailable from 13:25 to 14:20 UTC because of a log collection outage. This covers the reported time and prevents review of process creation and command-line evidence on the alerted host.
Proxy and network records show connections and requests, but do not establish that a downloaded file was executed.
claims_not_established: Whether PowerShell actually ran on WS-ARUIZ-01 at approximately 13:40 UTC, and, if so, its command line, parent process, user context, or purpose.
Whether the retrieved u.ps1 file was the cause of the reported window or was executed at all.
Whether the raj.patel network logon from WS-ARUIZ-01 was authorized or related to the reported PowerShell activity.
Whether any account or host was compromised.
additional_evidence_needed: Recover or obtain endpoint process creation, PowerShell operational/script-block, and command-line telemetry for WS-ARUIZ-01 around 13:20–14:20 UTC, if available from another source.
Obtain the contents and provenance of the retrieved u.ps1 file and determine whether it was saved or executed on WS-ARUIZ-01.
Validate with raj.patel whether the 13:37 network logon to WS-RPATEL-01 from WS-ARUIZ-01 was expected, and investigate the associated authentication activity.
unrelated_findings: WS-ARUIZ-01 accessed dash.cloudflare.com, including the /domains page and an API zones endpoint; review separately against the approved-service inventory (T063-00203, T063-00204, T063-00232, T063-00244).

WS-ARUIZ-01 made SMB connections to DC-PIN-01, including a subsequent NTLM ANONYMOUS LOGON; investigate separately, without treating it as evidence that decides this alert (T063-00310, T063-00322, T063-00326).

WS-ARUIZ-01 established TLS connections to WS-TWEBER-01; the records identify the destination but do not establish the application or purpose, so review separately (T063-00121, T063-00123, T063-00333, T063-00335).
